title: Relativistic Algebra over Finite Ring Continuum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$ with primitive roots; $\gen^{\p-1}=1$; $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (Euler's criterion); the affine maps $x\mapsto a+bx$, $b\neq0$, are the bijections preserving the field structure up to relabelling.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The sign of the quarter-turn exponent: the oriented quarter-turn is $\im=\gen^{-\kap}=-\gen^{\kap}$, the exponent negative by pullback covariance (00:C7); the positive-exponent reading is the conjugate chart. Declared here, derived in the corpus.

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shell, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the Subject's frame $(\tau;0,1,\gen)$ with $\gen$ a primitive root and the drive $x\mapsto\gen x$; the cycle $\Phi_\p\cong C_{\p-1}$; $\im:=-\gen^{\kap}$ (A2), $-1=\gen^{2\kap}$. Replaces ``radius $\chron$'' and ``$\Fp(0,1)$''.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Symmetry completeness (Thm.~\ref{thm:symmetric-completeness} restated): the fourth roots of unity form the unique order-four subgroup $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$; under the Klein four-group $\langle x\mapsto-x,\,x\mapsto x^{-1}\rangle$, $Q_4$ is the union of the two size-two orbits $\{\pm1\}$, $\{\pm\im\}$, and $\Fpx\setminus Q_4$ splits into exactly $\kap-1$ orbits of size four. For $\p\equiv3\pmod4$ no $\im$ exists.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The oriented quarter-turn: $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$ satisfies $\im^{2}=-1$ for every primitive root $\gen$; the two square roots of $-1$ are $\{-\gen^{\kap},\gen^{\kap}\}$, so the drive fixes which is $\im$. On $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$: $\im=5$.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Affine reframing (Def.~\ref{def:framed-field} corrected, Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-invariance}): $\varphi_{a,b}(x)=a+bx$, $b\neq0$, is a ring isomorphism $(\Fp,+,\cdot)\to(\Fp,\oplus,\otimes)$ with origin $a$ and unit $a+b$ (not $b$); every polynomial identity is frame-covariant.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Origin and unit are observer data (affine gauge); the generator $\gen$ is the Subject's drive, not gauge; the observer's window is the naturals below $\sqrt\p$ (00:B8). Replaces ``$H\ll\It=\sqrt{\p-1}$'' (Section~\ref{sec:unification}).

blocks.title: Arithmetic symmetries and the orbital complex

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The four symmetries as maps of the shell: the successor $C_1:k\mapsto k+1$; translations $T_a$, $a\in\Fp$, the cycle $C_\p$; scalings $S_m$, $m\in\Fpx$, the cycle $C_{\p-1}$; power maps $P_\varepsilon:x\mapsto x^{\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in C_{\p-1}$, bijective iff $\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)=1$.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The frame group (Prop.~\ref{prop:frame-group}): $\langle T_a,S_m\rangle$ is the affine group of order $\p(\p-1)$, acting simply transitively on the frames $(a,b)$, $b\neq0$; the set of frames is a torsor under it (00:C5, 00:Y3).

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Meridians and latitudes (Def.~\ref{def:orbit-sphere}): $M_n(a)=a\gen^{n}$, $a\in\Fp$, the ordered list of the shell with step $\gen^{n}$; $L_a(m)=a\gen^{m}$, $m\in C_{\p-1}$, $a\neq0$, the multiplicative cycle from $a$; the orbital complex $\Sp$ with vertex set $\{(n,\pm a)\}\cup\{0\}$. The $2$-sphere reading is 2-geometry's~\cite{akhtman2025geometry}.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Involutions and counts (Def.~\ref{def:orbit-sphere}\,(a)--(c)): $M_n(a)=M_{n+2\kap}(-a)$ and $L_a(m)=L_{-a}(m+2\kap)$ since $\gen^{2\kap}=-1$; $\p-1$ distinct meridian lists in $2\kap$ great circles; $2\kap$ latitude pairs; one-sided vertex count $(\p-1)^{2}/2+1$, the double cover $(\p-1)^{2}$ (00:B11).

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: Framed integers (Def.~\ref{def:integers} restated): the window $W_H=\{z\in\Z:|z|\le H\}$, $2H<\p$, embedded by $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$; sign, order and magnitude are the window's; sums read back for $4H<\p$, products for $2H^{2}<\p$ --- the corpus window $\sqrt\p$ (00:B1).

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The window law: $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$ is injective on $W_H$ when $2H<\p$; for $x,y\in W_H$ the residue of $x\pm y$ reads back the integer when $4H<\p$, and that of $xy$ when $2H^{2}<\p$ (the same injectivity on the windows $2H$ and $H^{2}$).

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Framed rationals (Def.~\ref{def:rationals} restated): $a/b$ with $a,b\in W_H$, $b\not\equiv0$, of value $ab^{-1}\in\Fp$; the scale grid $[x,n]:=x\gen^{-n}$, $x\in\{0,\dots,\p-1\}$, $n\in C_{\p-1}$; $G_n$ the ordered list $(x\gen^{-n})_x$, the meridian $M_{-n}$ of C3.

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Scale-periodicity (Lemma~\ref{thm:scale-periodicity}, restated in the field): $S_n(x)=x\gen^{-n}$ satisfies $S_{n+(\p-1)}=S_n$; the grids $G_n$ are $(\p-1)$-periodic as ordered lists; the zoom $[x,n]\mapsto[x,n+1]$ has order $\p-1$. As lists of rationals $x/\gen^{n}$ ($\gen$ lifted to $\Z$) the grids are not periodic: the periodicity is a relation of the field.

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: The chart of the grid [chart] (Prop.~\ref{prop:r-rationals}, Thm.~\ref{thm:approx} replaced): with $\gen$ lifted to an integer $\ge2$, every real $r$ with $|r|\le H\gen^{-n}$ lies within $1/(2\gen^{n})$ of some $x/\gen^{n}$, $x\in W_H$: resolution and range trade off at fixed window. Every real to every precision is unavailable: at $(13,2)$ no point of step $\le1/8$ lies within $1/16$ of $33/10$.

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The continuum as chart (Def.~\ref{def:reals}, Props.~\ref{prop:total-bounded}--\ref{prop:compactness}, Cor.~\ref{cor:knowability} retired): the framed real line is the reading of the nested grids against $\R$, a labelled idealisation entered nowhere as an object (00:B1); no completion, compactness or ``complete continuum'' is claimed.

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The framed complex chart (Def.~\ref{def:complex} restated): the pair $(a,b)\in W_H^{2}$ read as $a+b\im\in\Fp$; the quarter-turn acts on the shell as the rotation $x\mapsto\im x$ of order four; the chart is the plane picture of $Q_4$ acting on the shell, not an extension of $\Fp$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: The extension by $X^{2}+1$ is trivial (Prop.~\ref{prop:Cp-field} reversed): on the shell $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)\cong\Fp\times\Fp$ has zero divisors, $(X+\im)(X-\im)=0$, so it is not a field; $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)$ is a field exactly when $\p\equiv3\pmod4$; the quadratic extension of the shell is $\Fp[\eta]$, $\eta^{2}=\nu$ a non-square (8-dirac B6).

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: No element of additive order two (Thm.~\ref{thm:no-south-pole}): $2s=0$ forces $s=0$; the antipode of the origin on the additive cycle is not a residue; it sits between $2\kap=(\p-1)/2$ and $2\kap+1=(\p+1)/2=2^{-1}$ (20-rh B8).

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The antipode named $\infty$: the horizon of the observer at $0$ (00:Y3), the compactification point of the framed line [chart]; its reading as classical infinity is the chart, not a residue.

Ten \textsf{EXACT}, one \textsf{CHART}.

rows.label: V2
rows.predicate: \texttt{reports/lean/Algebra.lean} (the corpus tree), Lean~4.34, Mathlib 15~Sep~2026: fourteen theorems for every finite field of cardinality $4\kap+1$ --- B3, B4, D4, F1 complete; B2, C4, D2, E2 with a counting or converse clause outstanding; the $\F_{13}$ instance of B3; Lemma~\ref{lem:euclid-bound} refuted by \texttt{decide}, the obstruction to Thm.~\ref{thm:approx} proved over $\Q$. rows.label: O1
rows.predicate: The conjecture of the conclusion: the finite substrate supports polynomial equation solving, limit-like approximation and $\varepsilon$-approximation of continuous symmetries. Stated without proof; the transform layer (6-fourier) and the Cayley steps (8-dirac) discharge parts of it; the general statement remains open.
